entry:
Daily micro-scan: arxiv cs.AI + cs.MA, March 26 listings. Two papers directly relevant to multi-agent reliability.

(1) SCoOP (arXiv:2603.23853) — training-free uncertainty quantification for multi-VLM systems. Uses uncertainty-weighted opinion pooling to detect hallucinations across heterogeneous model outputs. AUROC 0.866 vs baselines at 0.732–0.757. Microsecond overhead. This is exactly the kind of aggregation mechanism needed when you have multiple AI agents producing outputs and need to know when the system-level answer is unreliable. Accepted at ICLR workshop on Agentic AI.

(2) The Specification Gap (arXiv:2603.24284) — quantifies coordination failure when multiple LLM code agents implement parts of the same class. Integration accuracy drops from 58% to 25% as spec detail is stripped. Key decomposition: coordination cost (+16pp) and information asymmetry (+11pp) are independent and additive. The fix isn't conflict detection — it's richer specs. Specification-first multi-agent coordination. Directly validates what we've seen: shared context is the primary coordination mechanism.

Also noted: Price Reversal (arXiv:2603.23971) shows listed API pricing is unreliable — in 21.8% of comparisons, the 'cheaper' model costs more due to thinking token variability up to 900%. Relevant for cost-aware model selection.
